column6: When should a rec:Collection be used?
column7: rec:Collection | Collection < rdfs:Resource :: An administrative grouping of entities that are adressed and treated as a unit for some purpose. These entities may have some spatial arrangement (e.g., an apartment is typically contiguous) but that is not a requirement (see, e.g., a distributed campus consisting of spatially disjoint plots or buildings). Inclusion in a Collection is determined by the 'includes' field on a specific subclass.

column6: Which direct subclasses does brick:Equipment have?
What is a rec:Asset?
column7: rec:Asset | Asset < rdfs:Resource :: Something which is placed inside of a building, but is not an integral part of that building's structure; e.g., furniture, equipment, systems, etc.

column6: What is a brick:Sensor?
column7: brick:Sensor | Sensor < brick:Point :: A Sensor is an input point that represents the value of a device or instrument designed to detect and measure a variable (ASHRAE Dictionary).

column6: Is brick:Building a direct subclass of brick:Location?
column7: brick:Building | Building < brick:Location :: An independent unit of the built environment with a characteristic spatial structure, intended to serve at least one function or user activity [ISO 12006-2:2013]

column6: What does the rec:Portfolio definition list as groupable members?
column7: rec:Portfolio | Portfolio < rec:Collection :: A portfolio is a grouping of buildings, sites, apartments, campuses, etc. that share some business-relevant commonality, e.g., are managed by the same company, are rented out to the same tenant, share utilization or legal definition (industrial vs commercial), etc.

column6: Which top-level classes are direct subclasses of brick:Point?
column7:
brick:Alarm | Alarm < brick:Point :: Alarm points are signals (either audible or visual) that alert an operator to an off-normal condition which requires some form of corrective action
brick:Command | Command < brick:Point :: A Command is an output point that directly determines the behavior of equipment and/or affects relevant operational points.
brick:Parameter | Parameter < brick:Point :: Parameter points are configuration settings used to guide the operation of equipment and control systems; for example they may provide bounds on valid setpoint values
brick:Sensor | Sensor < brick:Point :: A Sensor is an input point that represents the value of a device or instrument designed to detect and measure a variable (ASHRAE Dictionary).
brick:Setpoint | Setpoint < brick:Point :: A Setpoint is an input value at which the desired property is set
brick:Status | Status < brick:Point :: A Status is input point that reports the current operating mode, state, position, or condition of an item. Statuses are observations and should be considered 'read-only'

column6: What is a brick:Zone?
column7: brick:Zone | Zone < brick:Location :: (1) a separately controlled heated or cooled space. (2) one occupied space or several occupied spaces with similar occupancy category, occupant density, zone air distribution effectiveness, and zone primary airflow per unit area. (3) space or group of spaces within a building for which the heating, cooling, or lighting requirements are sufficiently similar that desired conditions can be maintained throughout by a single controlling device.

column6: Which property states the primary function of a Building?
column7: OP brick:buildingPrimaryFunction

column6: Which property expresses spatial containment of an entity in a location?
column7: OP brick:hasLocation inv:brick:isLocationOf

column6: How does the schema advise handling rec:ArchitectureArea measurements?
column7: rec:ArchitectureArea | Architecture area < rec:Information :: Describes business-relevant area measurements typically associated with architected spaces. As the exact requirements on these measurements will vary from case to case or jurisdiction to jurisdiction, subclassing and specializing this definition is encouraged.

column6: How should deprecated terms be handled in Brick?
column7: DP brick:deprecationMitigationMessage

column6: What organizations does the rec:Organization definition cite?
column7: rec:Organization | Organization < rec:Agent :: An organization of any sort (e.g., a business, association, project, consortium, tribe, etc.)

column6: Which property records a building's gross floor area?
column7: OP brick:grossArea

column6: Which events does the rec:Event definition give as examples?
column7: A temporally indexed entity, e.g., an observation, a lease, a construction project, etc.

column6: Which property attaches a unit to a Quantity or Point?
column7: OP brick:hasUnit

column6: What does rec:PointEvent exemplify?
column7: rec:PointEvent | Point event < rec:Event :: An event emanating from or targeting a Point; e.g., an individual Observation from a Sensor point, or an Actuation sent to a Command point. In other terms, the Points indicate the capability of some Space or Equipment to emit or accept data, while this class represents those actual data messages.

column6: How is a virtual metering hierarchy modeled?
Where is the most recent observed value of a Point stored?
column7: OP brick:lastKnownValue

column6: What is the inverse of brick:hasPart?
column7: OP brick:hasPart inv:brick:isPartOf

column6: What containment example does the rec:Space definition give?
column7: rec:Space | Space < rdfs:Resource :: A contiguous part of the physical world that contains or can contain sub-spaces. E.g., a Region can contain many Sites, which in turn can contain many Buildings.

column6: What does rec:Georeference express?
column7: rec:Georeference | Georeference < rec:Information :: A georeference creates a relationship between a local coordinate system into a geographic coordinate system.

column6: What is a rec:Campus?
column7: rec:Campus | Campus < rec:Collection :: A campus represents a collection of location entities. The constituent locations may have differing legal ownership and utilization purposes, but they are generally perceived as a coherent unit or sub-region within a city or other region. E.g., a university campus, a hospital campus, a corporate campus, etc.

column6: Which property records when something was built?
column7: DP brick:yearBuilt

column6: What relates a brick:Equipment to the tags it carries?
column7: OP brick:hasTag inv:brick:isTagOf

column6: Which property links a Brick entity to an external vocabulary reference?
column7: OP ref:hasExternalReference

column6: How are measurement quantities represented on Points?
Which classes are direct subclasses of brick:Location?
What does brick:Meter represent?
column7: brick:Meter | Meter < brick:Equipment :: A device that measure usage or consumption of some media --- typically a form energy or power.

column6: Are Alarm and Sensor disjoint in Brick?
column7: brick:Alarm | Alarm < brick:Point

column6: What relates an Equipment or Point to its Location?
column7: OP brick:hasLocation inv:brick:isLocationOf

column6: Which entities does the rec:BuildingElement definition list as examples?
column7: rec:BuildingElement | Building element < rdfs:Resource :: A part that constitutes a piece of a building's structural makeup. E.g., Facade, Wall, Slab, Roof, etc.

column6: How is a Point linked to the quantity it measures?
column7: OP brick:hasQuantity

column6: Which property pair expresses supply/feed direction?
column7: OP brick:feeds inv:brick:isFedBy

column6: How do you express that a Point belongs to an Equipment?
column7: OP brick:isPointOf inv:brick:hasPoint
